title: The day God called him… Jeremiah tried to say no.
paragraphs: The day God called him… Jeremiah tried to say no.

Not because he didn’t believe in God.
Not because he didn’t care about truth.
But because he looked at himself… and saw weakness.

Too young.
Too untrained.
Too afraid.
And if we’re honest, that is exactly where many of us live.

We read about prophets, apostles, and missionaries.
We hear sermons about boldness and courage.
And quietly inside we whisper:
“That could never be me.”
But Jeremiah 1 shatters that lie.
Because the story of Jeremiah does not begin with a strong man.
It begins with a God who chooses trembling people.
Listen to the thunder of this verse:

“Before I formed you in the womb I knew you,
before you were born I set you apart;
I appointed you as a prophet to the nations.”
— Jeremiah 1:5
Pause for a moment and feel that.

Before Jeremiah had a voice…
God already had a purpose.

Before Jeremiah preached one sermon…
God already knew his name.

Before Jeremiah took his first breath…
God had already written the mission.
This is not random existence.
This is divine intention.
But here is the part that makes Jeremiah so human.

When God revealed the calling…
Jeremiah didn’t celebrate.
He panicked.

“Ah, Lord GOD! Behold, I do not know how to speak, for I am only a youth.”
— Jeremiah 1:6
Have you ever felt that?
When you sense God asking something of you…

• Speak truth.
• Turn away from sin.
• Share the Gospel.
• Lead your family.
• Stand for righteousness.
And suddenly fear rises like a wall inside your chest.
“I’m not ready.”
“I’m not strong enough.”
“I don’t know what to say.”
“I’ll fail.”
Jeremiah felt that same fear.
But God did not cancel the calling.
Instead, God answered the fear.

“Do not say, ‘I am only a youth.’
Do not be afraid…
for I am with you and will rescue you.”
— Jeremiah 1:7–8
Notice something powerful here.
God did not say:
“Jeremiah, you’re actually very talented.”
He didn’t say:
“Jeremiah, you’ll succeed because you’re confident.”
No.
God gave Jeremiah something far stronger than self-belief.
He gave him God’s presence.
“I am with you.”
That changes everything.
Then comes one of the most intimate moments in all of Scripture.

“Then the LORD reached out his hand and touched my mouth and said to me, ‘I have put my words in your mouth.’”
— Jeremiah 1:9
Imagine the moment.

A young man.
Afraid.
Overwhelmed.

And the Creator of heaven reaches out…
and touches his lips.
Jeremiah’s strength did not come from skill.
It came from a divine touch.
And that is still how God works today.
He does not wait for perfect people.

He calls the fearful.
He restores the broken.
He uses the unlikely.
But we must be honest about something.
Jeremiah’s calling was not glamorous.

He preached to people who rejected him.
He warned a nation that mocked him.
He spoke truth in a culture that hated truth.
Following God is not always applause.
Sometimes it is loneliness.
Sometimes it is misunderstanding.
Sometimes it is standing alone with truth when the world runs the other direction.
But Jeremiah’s story points us to someone even greater.
Because centuries later… another man would come who was also known, chosen, and sent.
Not just a prophet.
The Savior.
Jesus Christ.

Where Jeremiah trembled, Jesus stood perfect.
Where Jeremiah spoke God’s words, Jesus is the Word.
Where Jeremiah warned of judgment, Jesus stepped into judgment for sinners like us.
On the cross, Christ carried our rebellion.

Our shame.
Our fear.
Our failure.
And three days later… the grave lost.
Sin lost.
Death lost.
Grace won.
So the greatest truth is not simply that God knew Jeremiah before birth.
The greater miracle is this:
Jesus knows you in your sin… and still offers redemption.
Maybe today you feel disqualified.
Maybe your past whispers accusations.
Maybe fear keeps you silent.
But hear the voice of God that echoed through Jeremiah’s life:
“Do not be afraid… for I am with you.”
Your weakness does not cancel God’s power.
Your fear does not silence God’s purpose.
And your story is not finished yet.
Because the same God who calls prophets…
rescues sinners.
And the cross proves it.
If this message stirred something in you…
Someone in your circle right now is living under the lie that they are forgotten.
They need to hear this truth:

God sees.
God calls.
God redeems.
And in Jesus, even the most broken story can become a testimony of grace.
